---
title: "Before the day"
---

Three things are needed before the day, and each ends in something that you can check: R and the workspace installed, with the setup check printing OK; the first module on R worked through; and the background page read. The modules on the IDE, on Quarto and on Git and GitHub are recommended for anyone who would rather meet the tools at their own pace than on the day. The day itself is worked in the workspace, and a machine on which the installation failed can still follow every task in the deck of the day, whose slides run R inside your browser with the data already in place, or in the browser lab, a page of the course site that holds the same tasks.

## 1. R and the workspace

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the workspace zip, and run `R/check_setup.R` until it prints OK. You do this once, and the workspace is yours to keep after the day. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met. If the installation will not cooperate, tell the facilitator before the day, and follow the day in the deck and the browser lab.

## 2. Getting started with R

[Open Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The module teaches the R that the tasks of the day ask of you, from a first line of code to a share of replies, a difference between two shares, a table and a figure, all on the data of this case study. Its blocks of code run in your browser, so it can be worked before the installation, alongside it, or on a machine on which you cannot install anything.

## 3. Background {#the-case-study}

[Read the background](../../cases/housing/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The background page presents the original study and its design, SCORE and its robustness study (Multi100; Aczel et al. 2026), the five reanalyses and the question that each of them answered, how their results were put on one scale, and the replication with new data. Every part of the day works on this case study.

## 4. The browser lab

[Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The browser lab is the fallback of the day if your installation fails. Open it once on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait until the first cell shows a "Run Code" button, and run the setup cell of Task 1. If it does not load, try another browser, and tell the facilitator before the day.

## 5. Further preparation

The modules on [the IDE (Positron and other IDEs)](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html), on [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) and on [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) take the tools of the workspace further, each with tasks in the workspace of this case study. The [exercise](exercise.qmd) page sets out the claim that you will be working on, the five tasks with the tool in which each is done, and the table of what the five analysts of the robustness study found when they reanalysed it.

**By the start of the day** you have the setup check printing OK, or the browser lab loading on the machine that you will use, you have worked through the first module on R, and you know what the claim is and how the five analysts of the robustness study came to different conclusions about it.
